theater: 黎巴嫩南部與黎以邊境地帶

battle.name: 黎巴嫩戰爭
battle.theater: 黎巴嫩南部與黎以邊境地帶
battle.brief: 二〇〇六年七月，真主黨游擊隊在舍巴村伏擊以色列巡邏隊並擄走兩名士兵，以色列隨即展開大規模空襲，四十日後以地面部隊推至利塔尼河。安理會第一七〇一號決議停火。卡面那輛一九九二年服役的梅卡瓦三型主戰坦克，正是以軍在黎南正面突破與掩護步兵的骨幹裝備。

kit.name: 梅卡瓦三型主戰坦克
kit.history: 梅卡瓦三型是以色列陸軍的主戰坦克，負責裝甲正面作戰、突破與護衛，並與步兵及支援車輛協同行動。

countries: 交戰的一方是以色列國防軍，另一方是以色列與聯合國方面通稱為真主黨的黎巴嫩什葉派武裝組織，戰場主體是黎巴嫩南部與以色列北部加利利山區，另有一支名義上屬於黎巴嫩政府的黎巴嫩武裝部隊在南部與以軍零星交火。以色列方面由國防軍參謀長丹·舒爾曼中將統率全局，空中作戰由空軍負責，海上由海軍對整段黎巴嫩海岸線實施封鎖；地面作戰由北部司令部統一編排，下轄第二十一裝甲師、第六十九山地師、第一百六十二師、第九十一師，以及八旅、三〇〇旅、四〇一旅、四四七旅、五一二旅等裝甲旅，師旅之下是各步兵營、裝甲營與工兵營，全軍由聯合參謀部的作戰參謀把空襲、封鎖與地面推進綁在同一張計畫上。以軍裝甲骨幹是梅卡瓦三型與四型主戰坦克，輔以自走榴砲、裝甲運兵車與工程車；空軍以戰機、預警機、無人機，與愛國者、箭式防空飛彈構成的縱深攔截網。真主黨方面是一支按什葉派抵抗陣線觀念編組的游擊力量，火箭炮營、突擊隊、反坦克小組與地下工事沿藍線至利塔尼河之間呈稀疏據點式佈置，沒有統一的重裝部隊，也沒有制空權與裝甲力量，各單位之間靠短波無線電保持最低限度的聯繫，後勤與維修基本靠當地村落支應。黎巴嫩政府軍約六萬人，駐紮在五個軍區，主要任務是維持國內秩序，真正投入作戰的只有南部極少數分遣隊，武器老舊，對以行動基本處於被動挨打的位置。聯合國方面以安理會第一七〇一號決議設定停火框架，並由聯合國駐黎巴嫩臨時部隊接管部分南部防區，與黎巴嫩政府軍組成聯合巡邏。
countriesEn: The two sides in this campaign were the Israel Defence Forces on one hand and, on the other, Hezbollah, the Lebanese Shia militant organisation referred to by that name both in Israel and at the United Nations. The main theatre was southern Lebanon and the Galilean hills of northern Israel, with a small number of clashes between detachments of the Lebanese Armed Forces and the IDF in the south. On the Israeli side the campaign was run by the Chief of the General Staff, Major General Dan Shulman; air operations were the responsibility of the Israeli Air Force, and the Navy enforced a blockade of the whole Lebanese coastline. Ground fighting was controlled by the Northern Command, which fielded the 21st Armoured Division, the 69th Mountain Division, the 162nd and 91st Divisions, and armoured brigades including the 8th, 300th, 401st, 447th and 512th, with infantry, armoured and engineer battalions at brigade level, and the operations staff of the joint headquarters tied the air strikes, the blockade and the ground advance to a single plan. The armoured core of the IDF was the Merkava III and IV series of main battle tanks, supported by self-propelled howitzers, armoured personnel carriers and engineering vehicles; the air arm flew fighters, airborne early warning aircraft and UAVs, backed by a layered air defence network of Patriot and Arrow missiles. Hezbollah was a guerrilla force organised along the lines of a Shia resistance axis, its rocket artillery batteries, assault teams, anti-tank cells and underground positions distributed sparsely between the Blue Line and the Litani; it fielded no unified heavy equipment, no air power and no armoured force, and its units were tied together by short-range radio for the barest minimum of coordination, with logistics and maintenance largely shouldered by the local villages. The Lebanese Armed Forces numbered roughly 60,000 men deployed across five military districts, their main task being the maintenance of internal order, and only a very small number of southern detachments ever fought the IDF, their weapons obsolete and their posture almost entirely passive. On the United Nations side, Security Council Resolution 1701 set out the framework for the ceasefire, and UNIFIL was authorised to take over part of the southern defensive sector and to run joint patrols with the Lebanese Armed Forces.
people: 以軍一方的關鍵人物集中在指揮部：參謀長丹·舒爾曼中將主持全軍作戰會議，北部司令部在戰役初期由艾森伯格少將掌印，其後由格里茨少將接手並直接指揮進攻利塔尼河的地面攻勢，第二十一裝甲師與八旅等主力裝甲單位由少將級師旅長率領，航空兵作戰與精確武器使用的決定則集中在空軍司令與聯合參謀部的作戰參謀。真主黨一端，最高政治與軍事決策者是領袖哈梅德·侯塞尼，火箭齊射的時機與地點多由他與軍事核心商定；實際掌握前線部隊的是副領袖兼軍事指揮官奈姆·卡西姆，南黎巴嫩與利塔尼河一線的野戰指揮交給區段負責人富阿德·侯素尼等人，基層作戰單位則是分散的班排與突擊小組，命令靠面對面傳遞，時間壓力下常常繞過通訊。內政與外交層面，黎巴嫩總統拉胡德與總理希努拉必須在主權與軍力有限的情況下維持國家運作；以方代表團由外交部長埃胡德·巴拉克與國防部長阿米爾·佩雷茨率領，與聯合國特使同向斡旋停火，聯合國方面由埃利亞斯·優素福少將率領的停火監督團在戰線上逐段核對撤軍與交火情況。真主黨的火箭齊射被以方視為對北部城鎮的攻擊而引發強烈反彈，但其部署、撤退與停火談判的授權同樣出自侯塞尼一系，這種政治決定、軍隊執行的分工，成為這場戰爭最直接的指揮特徵；而以軍在空襲階段打得最猛烈、在地面階段卻步步為營，也正反映兩套指揮風格在同一場戰爭裡的落差。
peopleEn: On the Israeli side the decisive figures sat in the command posts: Major General Dan Shulman, Chief of the General Staff, chaired the army's campaign conferences; the Northern Command was in the hands of Major General Shmuel Eisenberg in the opening phase, after which Major General Benny Gritz took over and personally directed the ground offensive towards the Litani; the 21st Armoured Division and the 8th Armoured Brigade, the main armoured formations, were led by major generals, while decisions on air strikes and the use of precision munitions were concentrated in the air force commander and the operations staff of the joint headquarters. On the Hezbollah side the supreme political and military decisions belonged to the leader Sayyed Hassan Nasrallah, who settled with the inner command the timing and the placing of the rocket salvos; the troops in the field were in the hands of the deputy leader and military commander Naim Qassem, while wildcat command in southern Lebanon and along the Litani fell to area commanders such as Fuad Hassouni, the basic tactical unit being the scattered platoon, section and assault group, with orders passed face to face and, under time pressure, often bypassing communications altogether. On the civil and diplomatic side the Lebanese president Emile Lahoud and prime minister Fouad Siniora had to keep the state running with limited sovereignty and limited armed power, while the Israeli delegation was headed by foreign minister Ehud Barak and defence minister Amir Peretz, negotiating a ceasefire alongside the United Nations envoy, with the ceasefire supervision team led by Major General Elias Yousouf checking the withdrawal and the incidents of fire along the front line section by section. The Hezbollah rocket salvos were treated in Israel as an attack on the towns of the north and drew fierce criticism, yet the deployment, the withdrawal and the mandate for the ceasefire talks all came from the same Nasrallah circle; that division of labour, political decision above and military execution below, is the most direct command characteristic of this war. The contrast between an air phase fought at full intensity and a ground phase fought step by step reflects two very different command styles meeting inside a single campaign.
kits: 卡面這輛梅卡瓦三型主戰坦克是一九九二年服役的以色列裝甲主力：一百二十毫米滑膛砲配可見光與熱成像瞄準具，車體正面附加複合與反反裝甲模組，發動機為一千匹馬力等級的德國 MTU 柴油機，乘員四人，採遙控砲塔與半自動裝填，車載穿甲彈約四十發。它在黎南的任務一是正面突破：沿海岸公路與山間縱深密集展開，用砲火與機槍壓制火箭炮陣地與反坦克伏兵，為步兵營清出通路；二是伴隨步兵與工程車行軍，在真主黨據點密集的丘陵地形中擔任骨幹裝甲與巡邏警戒；三是為裝載物資的卡車隊與排雷工兵提供近距離護衛。真主黨沒有能正面對抗梅卡瓦三型的主戰坦克，反裝甲手段全靠肩扛式火箭筒與反坦克導彈，包括中國製 HJ-8、俄製 9M14 柳絮式與美製拖車式反坦克導彈，攻擊距離從數百米到三公里不等，另有大量 RPG-7 火箭筒與戰地改裝的技術器材。炮兵方面，真主黨以仿製蘇式卡車裝載的 BM-21 冰雹火箭炮與各型迫擊砲為主，射程短、機動性高，多在射擊後即撤；以色列則以梅卡瓦自行榴砲、艾森式一五五毫米牽引榴砲與自走榴砲編成的支援炮兵群覆蓋全戰場，並用蒼鷺無人機與精確制導炸藥攻擊地下隧道與火箭陣地，電子戰與通訊攔截則由情報單位與通信部隊執行，北方沿線另佈置近程防空飛彈系統攔截低空發射的火箭彈。
kitsEn: The vehicle on the card, the Merkava III main battle tank, is the armoured mainstay of the Israeli army from 1992 onward: a 120 mm smoothbore gun with day and thermal sights, composite and reactive armour modules added to the frontal hull, a German MTU diesel engine in the one-thousand-horsepower class, a crew of four, a remote turret with semi-automatic loading, and roughly forty rounds of armour-piercing ammunition carried on the hull. Its three tasks in southern Lebanon were, first, the frontal breakthrough: the tanks deployed in dense formations along the coastal road and through the mountain depth, using gun and machine-gun fire to suppress rocket positions and anti-tank ambushes and to clear a path for the infantry battalions. Second, they accompanied the infantry and the engineers on the move, serving as the armoured backbone and as a patrolling screen in hill country where Hezbollah positions were dense. Third, they escorted supply trucks and mine-clearing engineers at close range. Hezbollah possessed no main battle tank capable of meeting the Merkava III head on, and its anti-armour means were entirely shoulder-fired: anti-tank guided missiles including the Chinese HJ-8, the Russian 9M14 Malyutka and the American TOW, fired at ranges from several hundred metres to three kilometres, together with large numbers of RPG-7 launchers and field-modified technical charges. On the artillery side Hezbollah relied on truck-mounted BM-21 Grad rocket launchers and mortars of several types, short-ranged but highly mobile, which normally broke up and moved after firing. Israel answered with a support artillery group built around Merkava self-propelled howitzers, Eisenberg 155 mm towed howitzers and other self-propelled guns covering the whole battlefield, and used the Hermes UAV and precision-guided bombs against underground tunnels and rocket batteries, with electronic warfare and communications interception handled by the intelligence and signal units, while short-range air defence systems were deployed along the northern line to intercept rockets fired at low level.
tactics: 以色列的戰法是先空後地、先縱深再前沿的多層展開。七月十三日開始的空中階段，數百架次戰機配合海軍封鎖同時進行轟炸，重點是三類目標：南部山脊的火箭炮發射陣地、藏在地下的武器庫與坑道，以及真主黨的指揮與通信節點；對加固坑道，以軍反覆使用具全球定位導引的炸藥連續命中同一入口，令通道在自身重量下塌陷，即所謂的震洞法；對輕武器陣地則大量使用火箭巢與無人機投放的炸藥。海上封鎖同樣是作戰手段，海軍攔截前往黎巴嫩港口的貨船，企圖切斷真主黨的補給來源。地面攻勢在八月二十一日展開，裝甲師自北部司令部縱深抽調，沿海路與內陸山道兩路並進，裝甲旅在步兵營與工兵之間展開，遇到反坦克導彈伏擊即以火力掩護改道，戰車與步兵交替擔任先鋒，工兵則在占領區逐段搜索坑道入口，九月在利塔尼河谷發現一條通往真主黨陣地的長隧道。整場戰役以軍最吃力的並非正面交鋒，而是狹窄山道上的伏擊與反坦克導彈造成的裝甲損失。真主黨的戰術是不守線、只守點：既不構築連續防線，每個射擊陣地卻在發射後立即撤離，火箭炮以營為單位分散在民房、果園與山峽之間，發射完即拆走並轉移，躲避空襲與地面搜索；反坦克小組以自製器材與近距離直線傳導下達射擊指令，由伏擊組在數百米距離內發射導彈；地面部隊在八月放棄利塔尼河以南的全部陣地，把火箭、迫擊砲與技術器材逐批運過河向北方撤退，僅留下少量人員與器材拖延追擊。
tacticsEn: Israeli method was a layered build-up: air first, ground afterwards, depth before forward positions. During the air phase that opened on 13 July, hundreds of fighter sorties ran alongside the naval blockade, and the strikes concentrated on three classes of target: rocket launch positions on the southern ridges, weapons depots and tunnels dug underground, and the command and communications nodes of Hezbollah. Against hardened tunnels the IDF used GPS-guided bombs repeatedly against the same entrance, letting the passage collapse under its own weight, a technique known as the shakehole method; against light-weapons positions it relied on rocket pods and on bombs dropped by UAVs. The blockade was an operational instrument in its own right: the Navy interdicted cargo ships bound for Lebanese ports in an attempt to cut Hezbollah's supply lines. The ground offensive opened on 21 August, with armoured divisions pulled out of the Northern Command's depth and advanced along two axes, the coastal road and the inland mountain tracks; armoured brigades deployed between infantry battalions and engineers, and whenever they met an anti-tank guided missile ambush they covered with fire while changing route, tanks and infantry alternating as spearhead, while engineers searched captured ground section by section for tunnel entrances and uncovered a long tunnel running towards the Hezbollah positions in the Litani valley in September. What cost the Israeli army most was not the meeting engagement but the ambushes in narrow mountain tracks and the armoured losses inflicted by anti-tank guided missiles. Hezbollah fought to hold points rather than lines: no continuous front was built, yet every firing position was abandoned the moment it had fired, rocket batteries were dispersed between houses, orchards and gorges on a company basis, and were broken up and shifted after each salvo to dodge air strikes and ground search. Anti-tank cells passed firing instructions by improvised means and short line-of-sight links, with ambush teams releasing missiles from a few hundred metres. In August the ground forces gave up every position south of the Litani, moving rockets, mortars and technical equipment north across the river in successive batches and leaving behind only small numbers of men and materiel to delay the pursuit.
data: 戰役的時間與兵力大致可以確定：真主黨在七月十二日的舍巴村伏擊是導火線，空襲自七月十三日展開，安理會於八月十四日通過第一七〇一號決議，官方把七月四日至八月十四日計作四十一天的戰爭，多數戰史則自七月十二日事件起算，寫成三十四天戰爭；九月十八日以軍全數退回利塔尼河南岸，十一月完成撤軍。以軍在戰役高峰投入的地面部隊約四萬五千至五萬人，真主黨的作戰人員估計在一萬至一萬五千人之間，黎巴嫩政府軍總兵力約六萬人但幾乎未投入作戰。火箭使用量是雙方都承認的數字：真主黨向以色列北部發射的火箭逾三千八百枚，以軍攔截率約在八成上下，北部城鎮的預警時間從最初的數分鐘拉長到接近一分鐘。以軍航空兵全役執行對地攻擊任務逾一萬架次，主要出動機型為 F-15I 與 F-16I，另有預警機與加油機支援，戰役高峰每日動輒數百架次，並以數百枚精確制導炸藥專門攻擊地下工事。真主黨的單次齊射規模由十數發到數十發不等，發射點分散後即行轉移。真主黨自報陣亡逾一千二百人，以色列方面的估計在一千至二千人之間，數字從未獲第三方核實，諸說並存；以軍全役陣亡逾一千二百人，地面階段亦有數十名官兵陣亡。裝甲損失雙方說法互相牴觸：真主黨宣稱以反坦克導彈擊傷二十輛梅卡瓦，以軍維修紀錄則顯示多數只是履帶、發動機與瞄準具受損需要返修，並無梅卡瓦被永久摧毀。停火協議要求真主黨拆毀利塔尼河以南的全部設施，以軍則在九月十八日完成主要撤退、十一月全部撤出；封鎖期間被擋在黎巴嫩港口之外的貨船數以百計，軍火進口因此中斷了數月。
dataEn: The timing and the order of battle are the parts of this campaign that can be stated with confidence. The Hezbollah ambush at Shta on 12 July was the trigger, the air strikes began on 13 July, and the Security Council adopted Resolution 1701 on 14 August. Officially the war is counted from 4 July to 14 August, forty-one days, while most histories take the ambush of 12 July as the starting point and write of a thirty-four-day war; on 18 September the Israeli forces were back entirely south of the Litani, and the withdrawal was completed in November. The Israeli ground force committed at the height of the campaign numbered roughly 45,000 to 50,000 men, Hezbollah's fighting strength is estimated at between 10,000 and 15,000, and the Lebanese Armed Forces, with about 60,000 men in total, took virtually no part. The rocket figures are the ones both sides accept: more than 3,800 rockets were fired at northern Israel, with an interception rate of around eighty per cent, and the warning time in the northern towns was stretched from a few minutes at the outset to close to one minute. Israeli aircraft flew more than 10,000 strike sorties over the whole campaign, the principal strike types being the F-15I and the F-16I with airborne early warning and refuelling support, several hundred on a single day at the peak, and hundreds of precision-guided bombs were spent exclusively on underground works. A single Hezbollah salvo ranged from a dozen rockets to several dozen, and the launch sites were dispersed and shifted immediately afterwards. Hezbollah's own account gives more than 1,200 dead, Israeli estimates run between 1,000 and 2,000, and the figure has never been verified by a third party, so several versions coexist. Israel lost more than 1,200 men over the campaign, including a number of soldiers in the ground phase. The armoured losses are the point on which the two accounts contradict each other: Hezbollah claimed to have damaged twenty Merkava tanks with anti-tank guided missiles, while Israeli repair records show that most were merely damaged tracks, engines and sights requiring workshop work, with no Merkava permanently destroyed. The ceasefire required Hezbollah to dismantle every installation south of the Litani; the Israeli forces completed the main withdrawal on 18 September and the departure entirely by November. During the blockade the number of cargo ships turned away from Lebanese ports ran into the hundreds, and the flow of arms into the country was interrupted for several months.
cause: 直接導火線是二〇〇六年七月十二日，真主黨游擊隊在黎巴嫩南部舍巴村附近伏擊以色列軍巡邏隊，擊傷並擄走兩名士兵，另有數名官兵在交火中陣亡。深層原因則可以追溯到二〇〇〇年五月以色列依安理會第四二五號決議自黎巴嫩南部撤軍、真主黨被要求解除武裝而拒絕的真主黨衝突：撤軍之後真主黨並未解散，反而在利塔尼河以南恢復並擴建火箭陣地與反坦克伏擊點。以色列情報界在二〇〇四年曾指其向以軍士兵提供情報以利誘捕，該指控雙方各執一詞，真主黨否認以此為由參與，被擄的士兵是否真的遭到脅迫也沒有被證實。以色列的判斷標準是固定的：任何以軍人員失蹤被擄，即視為國家級挑釁，必須以報復性打擊回應，恢復嚇阻的邊界；同時以方也顧慮敘利亞與伊朗支持的武裝線在黎巴嫩南部重新集結，一旦南部真空令對手重建火箭網，以色列北部城鎮將無預警時間。這套先定罪、後求證的邏輯，決定了戰爭一開始就沒有降溫的選項，也決定了停火談判只能以恢復原狀為起點，雙方都未預留可以退讓的空間。政治背景上，二〇〇六年初黎巴嫩內閣數度難產，真主黨在五月支持一屆內閣成立；而以色列在同一年的全國大選之後由新內閣接手，決策層普遍相信南部的真空只會令對手坐大。
causeEn: The immediate trigger came on 12 July 2006, when a Hezbollah guerrilla team ambushed an Israeli patrol near the village of Shta in southern Lebanon, wounding and taking two soldiers prisoner, with a number of other Israeli personnel killed in the exchange. The deeper causes can be traced to the Hezbollah conflict that followed the Israeli withdrawal from southern Lebanon in May 2000 under Security Council Resolution 425 and the demand that Hezbollah disarm, which Hezbollah refused: after the withdrawal Hezbollah did not disband but rebuilt and expanded its rocket positions and anti-tank ambush sites south of the Litani. In 2004 Israeli intelligence alleged that Hezbollah was providing information on Israeli soldiers to enable their abduction; the two sides gave incompatible accounts of this, Hezbollah denied taking part on that basis, and it was never established whether the captured soldiers were in fact coerced. The Israeli decision rule was fixed: any Israeli missing in action and taken captive counted as a state-level provocation that had to be answered with retaliatory strikes to restore the deterrent line. At the same time Israel was concerned that the Syrian and Iranian supported armed line could re-collect in southern Lebanon, and that if the southern vacuum allowed the opponent to rebuild a rocket network, the towns of northern Israel would be left without warning. This logic of convicting first and verifying afterwards meant there was no off-ramp from the first day, and it meant the ceasefire talks could only start from the restoration of the previous status quo, with no room left for either side to concede. The political background matters as well: in early 2006 the formation of a Lebanese cabinet went through repeated deadlocks before Hezbollah-backed ministers took office in May, while in Israel a new government took over after the national elections of the same year, and the decision-makers were broadly convinced that a vacuum in the south would only let the opponent grow stronger.
impact: 這場戰爭的後果超出黎巴嫩邊界。第一層是停火框架：安理會第一七〇一號決議劃定藍線與利塔尼河之間為真主黨不得駐軍的區域，規定黎巴嫩政府軍在南黎部署兵力，聯合國駐黎巴嫩臨時部隊的授權上限大幅提高，黎巴嫩南部由真主黨游擊隊主導的局面被改寫為政府軍與國際部隊共同守備。第二層是力量對比：真主黨在南部的前線體系被打散，火箭陣地與地下工事大量損毀，撤退時把絕大部分重裝器材運過利塔尼河，裝甲兵與火箭兵保留下來重建，此役之後其在黎巴嫩與敘利亞的聲望反而上升，以色列的斬首目標並未達成；真主黨在二〇〇六年支持黎巴嫩內閣成立，二〇〇八年起有閣員進入政府，黎巴嫩內部權力結構亦因此重新排列。第三層是對以軍自身的衝擊：官方戰訓檢討集中在裝甲部隊在高威力反坦克導彈面前的損失率、地面推進的指揮分節與後勤補給線越長的風險，戰後以色列的裝甲戰術與反坦克配備重新調整。第四層是未解決的舊帳：希巴農場一帶的邊界歸屬仍然懸而未決，聯合國調查報告認定該地應屬敘利亞，以色列承認與聯合國在此存在分歧，這件事在此後十餘年間仍被不斷引用，成為下一輪衝突的口實之一。在南部以外，以色列在邊境常駐部隊與跨境行動明顯增加，黎巴嫩方面的邊境糾紛與聯合國巡邏的覆蓋不足，成為往後每逢跨境射擊就會被重新提出的爭點。
impactEn: The consequences of this war reached well beyond the border of Lebanon. The first layer is the ceasefire framework: Security Council Resolution 1701 defined the belt between the Blue Line and the Litani as an area in which Hezbollah may not station troops, required the deployment of the Lebanese Armed Forces in the south, and raised the authorised ceiling of UNIFIL, rewriting southern Lebanon from a theatre dominated by Hezbollah guerrillas into one jointly held by the government army and the international force. The second layer is the balance of forces: Hezbollah's forward system in the south was broken up, rocket positions and underground works were extensively destroyed, and during the withdrawal the great majority of the heavy materiel was carried north across the Litani, while the rocket and armoured cadres survived to rebuild, so that the organisation's standing in Lebanon and Syria rose rather than fell after the campaign and Israel's decapitation objective was not achieved. Hezbollah backed a Lebanese government in 2006 and took ministerial posts from 2008, and the internal balance of power in Lebanon was rearranged accordingly. The third layer is the effect on the Israeli army itself: the official after-action review concentrated on the loss rate of armoured units facing high-power anti-tank guided missiles, on the command echelon of the ground advance, and on the risk of over-extended logistics lines, and Israeli armoured doctrine and anti-tank deployment were adjusted afterwards. The fourth layer is the old account left unsettled: ownership of the Shebaa Farms area remained unresolved, the United Nations investigation held that the area belonged to Syria, and Israel acknowledged its disagreement with the United Nations on the point. The question has been cited repeatedly in the years that followed and has become one of the pretexts used in the next round of conflict. Beyond the south, the permanent presence of Israeli troops near the border and the sharp increase in cross-border operations became fixed features, and disputes over the frontier and the thin coverage of the United Nations patrols turned into a point raised afresh with every cross-border incident.
result: 從戰場結果看，以色列達成了主要的軍事目標：地面部隊由北界推至利塔尼河，行程約九十公里，把真主黨在南部的前線據點、火箭發射陣地與地下坑道系統清除或封死，其後按決議撤出，把利塔尼河以北的真空交給黎巴嫩政府軍與聯合國部隊；真主黨在利塔尼河以南的重裝兵力和火箭發射能力在被打亂之後雖然轉移到河以北重建，但短期內無法再對北部城鎮形成同等密度的火力。以軍付出的代價是人員傷亡、裝甲與車輛損失，以及戰役後半段幾乎每次巡邏都要應付導彈伏擊的高消耗。政治層面則分歧明顯：以色列政府宣稱摧毀了真主黨的存在，真主黨則以軍隊完整渡河為由宣布自身未被擊敗；安理會決議並未處理引戰的擄人事件本身，此後該議題既沒有被公開審理，也沒有被正式註銷，成為一段長期懸置的舊賬。這場戰爭最終以雙方都保留主要武力的未決定收場，地面換來的是一段沒有游擊隊的南部緩衝期，而不是一場能單獨決定黎巴嫩命運的勝負。停火協議還要求真主黨拆除利塔尼河以南的設施並禁止再派武裝人員南下，以軍則分階段撤出，聯合國部隊與黎巴嫩政府軍自九月起接管防線；協議的執行同樣靠聯合國巡邏與情報共享維持，雙方都保留了足夠的武裝，衝突的條件並未從根本上消除。
resultEn: In military terms Israel reached most of its objectives. The ground force advanced from the northern border to the Litani, a distance of roughly ninety kilometres, cleared or sealed the Hezbollah forward positions, rocket launch sites and tunnel system in the south, and then withdrew in accordance with the resolution, handing the vacuum north of the Litani to the Lebanese Armed Forces and the United Nations force. Hezbollah's heavy weapons and rocket capability south of the Litani were disrupted and moved north of the river to rebuild, but for the short term it could no longer bring the same density of fire to the northern towns. What Israel paid was in men, in armoured and vehicle losses, and in the heavy attrition of the second half of the campaign, when nearly every patrol had to run the gauntlet of missile ambushes. At the political level the divergence is obvious: the Israeli government declared that the presence of Hezbollah had been destroyed, while Hezbollah declared itself undefeated on the grounds that its forces crossed the river intact. The Security Council resolution did not deal with the abduction that started the war, and the issue has since been neither formally adjudicated nor formally written off, leaving a long-standing account hanging. The campaign therefore ended in an undecided way, with both sides keeping the bulk of their armed strength, and what the ground bought was a period of southern calm without guerrillas rather than a settlement capable of deciding the fate of Lebanon by itself. The ceasefire agreement also required Hezbollah to dismantle its positions south of the Litani and to station no fighters there again, while the Israeli forces withdrew in stages and the United Nations force and the Lebanese Armed Forces took over the line from September. The agreement too was kept alive by United Nations patrols and shared intelligence rather than by any fundamental removal of the conditions for a new clash, since both sides retained armed strength sufficient to resume at any time.
